## Validation rules and thresholds

Section 3 distinguishes records that cannot describe a real journey, which are excluded outright, from those implausible in a single attribute, which are retained as demand events but withheld from the statistics they would distort. The table below lists every rule applied, the threshold chosen, the number of records affected and whether the rule acts as a hard exclusion or a soft one.

## Descriptive analytics

![Taxi demand by hour of day, split into weekdays and weekends. ![Seasonal demand profile across the observation period, showing the amplitude between the quiet winter months and the summer peak.](assets/seasonal-demand-profile.png){#fig-seasonal-demand-profile fig-scap="Seasonal demand profile" fig-pos="H"}

![Demand against temperature, aggregated to four-hour windows. The association remains when windows are compared within the same time of day.](assets/demand-vs-weather.png){#fig-demand-vs-temperature fig-scap="Demand against temperature" fig-pos="H"}

![Demand against precipitation intensity, aggregated to four-hour windows.](assets/demand-vs-precipitation-intensity.png){#fig-demand-vs-precipitation-intensity fig-scap="Demand against precipitation intensity" fig-pos="H"}

![Demand against snowfall intensity, restricted to winter months. ## Resolution sensitivity results

Section 4.2 reports the direction of the resolution effects and the values at the decisive points. The two tables below give the complete sweeps, spatially across r5, r6, r7, community areas and census tracts at fixed four-hour windows, and temporally across one-hour, four-hour, eight-hour and daily windows at fixed H3 r6. Both report cell count, zero rate, mean demand, MAE, normalised MAE, RMSE and R² for each model. Note that these refits reuse the tuned configuration rather than repeating the search at every resolution, so they are comparable across resolutions but not directly against the holdout results in the main text.

*[Placeholder: spatial and temporal resolution sweep tables.]*
